body.asks: One engine on this machine, the interface mounted to it over a socket, nothing polled. Fable's attack, to be taken before building: any web page can open a socket to 127.0.0.1 and write the repository, so the host checks Origin and Host and refuses attach on the socket; two tools committing through the engine at once would mint the same ids and overwrite each other, so a change says the head it read and is refused where it moved; with polling gone the engine is blind to files written beside it, so the host watches each store's ref and renews; the engine's governance refuses wholes with no type, a session noting a gone holon, and a let-go a reader's root points at; explicit new ids land as moved; into is not needed, every holon being held; a home in memory dies with the host and is shared by every tab, better a gitignored folder; attaching nothing draws nothing, so the host writes the attachments; the socket needs close, error and reconnect. Fable's smallest whole step: the stores attached read only to the one engine, the host watching each ref and renewing, the interface writing only its home, the tools unchanged; the tools through the engine later, once a change carries its head.

name: One engine, the interface mounted to it
